symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, poor fuel economy
likely_causes: Vacuum leak, clogged fuel filter, faulty MAF sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for code P0171. 2. Inspect vacuum lines for leaks. 3. Check MAF sensor voltage. 4. Measure fuel pressure.

symptoms: Check engine light, engine vibration, loss of power
likely_causes: Worn spark plugs, faulty ignition coils, low fuel pressure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0300 code. 2. Perform spark plug visual inspection. 3. Test coil resistance. 4. Check fuel pressure.

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced performance, possible emissions failure
likely_causes: Failed catalytic converter, upstream O2 sensor fault, exhaust leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Read P0420 code. 2. Perform O2 sensor voltage sweep test. 3. Inspect exhaust for leaks. 4. Use temperature probe across cat to assess efficiency.

issue_name: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
symptoms: Check engine light, faint fuel odor
likely_causes: Loose gas cap, cracked EVAP hose, faulty purge valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0455. 2. Tighten or replace gas cap. 3. Perform smoke test on EVAP lines. 4. Test purge valve operation.

symptoms: Fluid spots under vehicle, low transmission fluid level, delayed gear engagement
likely_causes: Worn pan gasket, damaged pan bolts
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect under vehicle for fluid. 2. Check transmission fluid level. 3. Locate leak source around pan. 4. Verify fluid color and smell.

symptoms: Vibration in brake pedal during braking, uneven brake wear
likely_causes: Warped brake rotors, uneven pad wear
diagnostic_steps: 1. Visual inspect rotors for scoring or runout. 2. Measure rotor thickness and runout with dial indicator. 3. Check brake pad wear.

symptoms: Dim headlights, slow engine crank, warning light on dash
likely_causes: Aged battery, corroded terminals, charging system failure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Measure battery voltage at rest (should be >12.4V). 2. Load test battery. 3. Check terminal corrosion and tighten connections. 4. Verify alternator output.

symptoms: Clunking noise when driving over bumps, uneven tire wear
likely_causes: Worn strut mounts, degraded bushings
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform bounce test on front corners. 2. Inspect strut mounts for cracks or looseness. 3. Check for play in steering knuckles.

symptoms: Temperature gauge rising, steam from engine bay, coolant loss
likely_causes: Clogged radiator, stuck thermostat, low coolant level
diagnostic_steps: 1. Check coolant level and condition. 2. Inspect radiator for external blockage. 3. Test thermostat operation by monitoring coolant temperature rise after start. 4. Verify radiator fan activation.

issue_name: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit High
symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle when cold start
likely_causes: Faulty IAT sensor, wiring short, connector corrosion
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0113. 2. Measure sensor voltage at cold and hot conditions. 3. Inspect wiring harness for damage. 4. Replace sensor if out of spec.

issue_name: Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature
symptoms: Check engine light, low engine temperature, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Stuck open thermostat, low coolant level, faulty coolant temperature sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for DTC P0128. 2. Verify coolant level. 3. Measure coolant temperature with infrared thermometer while engine warms. 4. Compare sensor reading to actual temperature. 5. Remove thermostat and test its opening temperature in boiling water.

issue_name: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient Detected
symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, increased emissions, poor fuel economy
likely_causes: Clogged EGR passages, stuck closed EGR valve, vacuum leak in EGR circuit
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0401. 2. Perform visual inspection of EGR valve and passages for carbon buildup. 3. Apply vacuum to EGR valve to see if it opens. 4. Use a scan tool to command EGR valve open and monitor flow sensor reading. 5. Check vacuum lines for cracks.

symptoms: Check engine light, erratic speedometer, transmission shift issues
likely_causes: Faulty VSS, damaged wiring harness, dirty sensor tone ring
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve DTC P0500. 2. Use a multimeter to measure VSS voltage while rotating wheel. 3. Inspect wiring connector for corrosion. 4. Check tone ring for damage or debris.

symptoms: Check engine light, transmission gear slippage, delayed shifts
likely_causes: Failed TCM, wiring issues, low transmission fluid pressure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0700 and any related sub‑codes (e.g., P0705). 2. Verify transmission fluid level and condition. 3. Perform a wiring continuity check to TCM. 4. Use a professional scan tool to request TCM live data and test output signals.

issue_name: Airbag System Fault – Supplemental Restraint System Disabled
symptoms: Airbag warning light, no deployment in crash
likely_causes: Faulty airbag control module, broken wiring harness, deployed airbag previously
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0A20 and related codes. 2. Inspect airbag module connectors for corrosion. 3. Verify module power and ground voltage with a multimeter. 4. Perform a module self‑test using a dealership scan tool.

symptoms: Check engine light, engine may run richer, minor fuel economy loss
likely_causes: Faulty knock sensor, wiring short to voltage, improper sensor gap
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0325. 2. Measure sensor voltage with engine off (should be ~0V) and at idle (should be low). 3. Check connector for water intrusion. 4. Compare resistance to spec.

issue_name: Throttle Actuator Control (TAC) Motor Circuit Range/Performance
symptoms: Check engine light, throttle feels unresponsive, jerky acceleration
likely_causes: Dirty throttle body, faulty throttle position sensor, TAC motor failure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P2101. 2. Inspect throttle body for carbon buildup; clean if needed. 3. Use scan tool to command throttle open/close and monitor position sensor voltage. 4. Check wiring for frays.

symptoms: Check engine light, oil leaks, rough idle
likely_causes: Clogged PCV valve, blocked breather hose, worn piston rings
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0C03. 2. Remove PCV valve and shake; audible rattle indicates good valve. 3. Inspect breather hose for blockages. 4. Perform compression test if high oil consumption persists.

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start, security light flashes
likely_causes: Faulty antenna ring, damaged key transponder, wiring fault
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P1500. 2. Verify key fob battery. 3. Inspect antenna ring wiring for damage. 4. Use dealer scan tool to perform immobilizer self‑test.

issue_name: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Too Low
symptoms: Check engine light, limited engine power, occasional stalling
likely_causes: Throttle motor weak, low supply voltage, wiring resistance
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P2108. 2. Measure supply voltage at throttle motor connector. 3. Compare motor current draw to specification while commanding open. 4. Inspect ground connection.

issue_name: Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) Sensor Circuit Low Voltage
symptoms: Rough idle, poor acceleration, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty MAP sensor, wiring harness damage, vacuum leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for code P0106. 2. Inspect MAP sensor connector for corrosion. 3. Measure sensor voltage with multimeter while engine is running (should be ~0.5-4.5V). 4. Compare voltage to live data via OBD scanner. 5. Test for vacuum leaks with smoke machine. 6. Replace sensor if voltage out of spec.

issue_name: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
symptoms: Check engine light, delayed catalytic converter warm-up, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Faulty O2 sensor heater, blown fuse, damaged wiring
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve code P0135. 2. Verify fuse for O2 sensor circuit. 3. Perform resistance check on sensor heater terminals (should be 2-5 ohms). 4. Use OBD live data to monitor sensor heating voltage. 5. Replace O2 sensor if heater resistance out of spec.

symptoms: Rough idle, loss of power, engine vibration, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty coil, bad spark plug, fuel injector issue, low compression
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0301. 2. Perform spark plug visual inspection; replace if fouled. 3. Swap coil with another cylinder and clear code; if code follows coil, replace coil. 4. Test fuel injector pulse with a scan tool. 5. Conduct compression test on cylinder 1.

symptoms: Stalling, dim headlights, check engine light, difficulty starting
likely_causes: Weak battery, failing alternator, poor ground connections
diagnostic_steps: 1. Read P0562 code. 2. Measure battery voltage with engine off (should be >12.4V). 3. Start engine and measure voltage at battery terminals (should be 13.5-14.5V). 4. Inspect battery terminals for corrosion. 5. Test alternator output with load tester.

symptoms: Parking brake light stays on, brake warning chime, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty switch, damaged wiring, corroded connector
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0584. 2. Locate parking brake switch under dashboard. 3. Check continuity of switch circuit with multimeter. 4. Inspect wiring harness for cracks or chafing. 5. Replace switch if continuity fails.

issue_name: Control Module Power Supply/ Ground Circuit Malfunction
symptoms: Harsh shifting, transmission slip, check engine light
likely_causes: Bad TCM power supply, corroded ground, blown fuse
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0610. 2. Check TCM fuse and relay. 3. Measure voltage at TCM power pin (should be ~12V). 4. Verify ground resistance (<5 ohms). 5. Scan for additional transmission codes. 6. Replace TCM if power/ground verified but fault persists.

symptoms: Hard shifts, delayed engagement, check engine light
likely_causes: Faulty shift solenoid, low fluid pressure, clogged valve body
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0706. 2. Check transmission fluid level and condition. 3. Perform solenoid resistance test (compare to spec). 4. Use scan tool to command shift and monitor response. 5. Replace solenoid if out of spec.

symptoms: Engine stalls, poor acceleration, check engine light
likely_causes: Weak fuel pump, clogged fuel filter, fuel pressure regulator failure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Read P1125. 2. Connect fuel pressure gauge to test port. 3. Measure pressure at idle (spec typically 30-45 psi). 4. Compare to spec. 5. Replace fuel filter, then retest. 6. If pressure still low, replace fuel pump.

symptoms: Black smoke, rough idle, fuel smell
likely_causes: Leaking fuel injector, faulty MAF sensor, vacuum leak, stuck open purge valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P2187. 2. Observe short-term fuel trim values via OBD; should be >+20% for rich condition. 3. Inspect MAF sensor for contamination; clean if dirty. 4. Perform fuel injector leak test (pressurized test). 5. Check for vacuum leaks with smoke machine. 6. Replace faulty component.

symptoms: Intermittent stalling, loss of power, check engine light
likely_causes: ECM overheating due to poor ventilation, water intrusion, failing cooling fan
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P2500. 2. Locate ECM and inspect for water or debris. 3. Verify cooling fan operation and airflow to ECM. 4. Measure ECM temperature sensor reading (if accessible). 5. Clean ventilation paths. 6. Replace ECM if temperature remains high.

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced power, higher emissions
likely_causes: Faulty catalyst, oxygen sensor malfunction, exhaust leak
diagnostic_steps:
1. Scan for stored codes and freeze frame data.
2. Perform a catalyst efficiency test with a scan tool.
3. Inspect exhaust system for leaks upstream of catalyst.
4. Test upstream and downstream O2 sensor voltages.
5. Replace catalyst if efficiency below 80% after confirming other causes.

symptoms: Rough idle, loss of power, engine vibration
likely_causes: Faulty spark plug, bad ignition coil, low compression
diagnostic_steps:
1. Retrieve live data for misfire count on cylinder 2.
2. Inspect and replace spark plug.
3. Swap coil with another cylinder to see if misfire follows.
4. Perform compression test on cylinder 2.
5. Replace faulty coil or address compression issue.

issue_name: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit High
symptoms: Check engine light, erratic fan operation, poor fuel economy
likely_causes: Short to voltage, damaged sensor wiring, failed sensor
diagnostic_steps:
1. Scan for P0118 and note freeze frame temperature.
2. Inspect sensor connector for corrosion or broken wires.
3. Measure sensor resistance at cold and hot states.
4. Replace sensor if resistance out of spec.
5. Clear codes and test drive.

symptoms: Check engine light, dim interior lights, intermittent stalling
likely_causes: Loose battery terminal, faulty alternator voltage regulator, bad wiring
diagnostic_steps:
1. Measure battery voltage with engine off (should be ~12.6V).
2. Start engine and measure voltage (should be 13.8‑14.8V).
3. Check alternator output and ground connections.
4. Inspect main power wire for damage.
5. Replace alternator or repair wiring as needed.

symptoms: Reduced electric assist, warning lights, limited driving range
likely_causes: Cell imbalance, high voltage fault, BMS failure
diagnostic_steps:
1. Use manufacturer-specific scan tool to read battery module voltages.
2. Identify modules outside tolerance.
3. Perform balance procedure if supported.
4. Replace faulty module or BMS if imbalance persists.
5. Clear codes and verify performance.

symptoms: Pulling to one side, brake pedal feels spongy, uneven wear
likely_causes: Corroded piston pin, collapsed brake hose, seized caliper slide pins
diagnostic_steps:
1. Inspect rear wheels for uneven pad wear.
2. Jack up vehicle, remove caliper, check piston movement.
3. Look for brake fluid leaks around caliper.
4. Replace caliper or rebuild with new seals and slide pins.
5. Bleed brake system and test.

symptoms: Clunking noise over bumps, poor handling, uneven tire wear
likely_causes: Worn rubber isolator, cracked metal mount
diagnostic_steps:
1. Perform bounce test on front corners.
2. Listen for metal‑on‑metal noise while driving over a speed bump.
3. Inspect strut mounts for cracks or looseness.
4. Replace mount if rubber is deteriorated.
5. Re‑align vehicle after replacement.

symptoms: Stalling, rough idle, no start after cranking
likely_causes: Damaged sensor, wiring harness chafing, poor connector contact
diagnostic_steps:
1. Scan for P0340 and check freeze frame data.
2. Visual inspection of sensor wiring for cracks.
3. Test sensor resistance and signal output with oscilloscope.
4. Replace sensor if out of spec.
5. Clear codes and perform start‑stop test.

symptoms: Fan runs continuously, battery drain, higher fuel consumption
likely_causes: Relay contacts welded, moisture ingress
diagnostic_steps:
1. Listen for fan operation with engine off and after start.
2. Test relay coil resistance and continuity.
3. Swap relay with identical one from another circuit.
4. Replace relay if faulty.
5. Verify fan cycles correctly with temperature sensor.

symptoms: Shift delays, limp mode, warning light
likely_causes: Faulty temperature sensor, low fluid level, clogged cooler
diagnostic_steps:
1. Scan for P0715 and note current sensor reading.
2. Check transmission fluid level and condition.
3. Test sensor resistance at known temperatures.
4. Replace sensor if out of spec.
5. Clear code and monitor for recurrence.

issue_name: Mass Air Flow Sensor Circuit Intermittent
symptoms: Rough idle, reduced power, stalling
likely_causes: Dirty MAF sensor, cracked wiring harness, faulty sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0101 code. 2. Inspect MAF sensor connector for corrosion or loose pins. 3. Measure voltage signal while engine runs (should fluctuate 0.5-4.5V). 4. Clean MAF sensor with MAF cleaner. 5. Replace sensor if voltage out of range.

symptoms: Engine stalls, no start, check engine light
likely_causes: Failed sensor, damaged wiring, connector corrosion
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0565 code. 2. Locate sensor on harmonic balancer. 3. Disconnect connector, test resistance (should be 500-1500 ohms). 4. Check for cracked wires or water intrusion. 5. Replace sensor if out of spec.

issue_name: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High Input
symptoms: Engine misfire, rough running, check engine light
likely_causes: Sensor voltage too high, short to power, wiring fault
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0335. 2. Verify sensor voltage with multimeter (should be 0-5V). 3. Inspect wiring for shorts to battery. 4. Replace sensor if voltage remains high after wiring correction.

issue_name: Transmission Input Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
symptoms: Gear shifting problems, transmission warning light, delayed engagement
likely_causes: Faulty sensor, damaged harness, connector corrosion
diagnostic_steps: 1. Read P0701 code. 2. Locate sensor on transmission input shaft. 3. Check connector pins for damage. 4. Measure sensor output while engine revs (should vary with RPM). 5. Replace sensor if output irregular.

symptoms: Black smoke, strong gasoline odor, decreased fuel economy
likely_causes: Leaking fuel injector, faulty O2 sensor, high fuel pressure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P1135. 2. Perform live data scan for short-term fuel trim (should be <+10%). 3. Inspect fuel injectors for leaks. 4. Test fuel pressure (should be within spec). 5. Replace leaking injector or O2 sensor as needed.

issue_name: Turbocharger Boost Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
symptoms: Loss of power, turbo lag, check engine light
likely_causes: Sensor failure, vacuum leak, wiring short to ground
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P1234 code. 2. Locate boost pressure sensor on turbo housing. 3. Measure sensor voltage (should be >0.5V). 4. Check for vacuum hose cracks. 5. Replace sensor if voltage low.

issue_name: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Failure (Front Left)
symptoms: ABS warning light, longer stopping distance, intermittent brake pedal feel
likely_causes: Sensor damage, corroded connector, broken tone ring
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform ABS self‑test via scan tool. 2. Visual inspection of sensor and tone ring for cracks. 3. Test sensor resistance (should be 800-1200 ohms). 4. Clean connector and pins. 5. Replace sensor if resistance out of range.

issue_name: Power Steering Fluid Leak from Reservoir Seal
symptoms: Whining noise when steering, low fluid level, occasional steering stiffness
likely_causes: Aged rubber seal, cracked reservoir, improper installation
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect reservoir for wet spots or dried fluid. 2. Check fluid level and condition. 3. Clean area and apply sealant if minor leak. 4. Replace reservoir if seal damaged.

issue_name: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Voltage
symptoms: Engine overheating, fan not engaging, check engine light
likely_causes: Sensor short to ground, damaged wiring, corroded connector
diagnostic_steps: 1. Locate coolant temperature sensor (usually on engine block). 2. Disconnect connector and measure resistance (should increase with temperature). 3. Check wiring for shorts to ground. 4. Replace sensor if resistance abnormal.

symptoms: Uncontrolled high idle, sudden acceleration, engine stall
likely_causes: Throttle actuator motor failure, carbon buildup, faulty control module
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform throttle position sensor (TPS) live data check (should move 0‑90%). 2. Inspect throttle body for carbon deposits; clean if needed. 3. Test voltage to throttle motor (12V). 4. If motor does not respond, replace throttle body assembly.
